Messages.Author: Brian Iverson
Messages.Body:
I may have already figured this one out, but I wanted to be sure and get
some other players opinions.

Here is the example of play:

Mike plays Minion Tap.
Brian plays Sudden Reversal to cancel the Minion Tap

Mike plays Sudden Reversal to cancel Brian's Sudden Reversal.

Is that a legal play? We finally decided that it was, and that the
Minion Tap was successful.
The only thing I was not sure about is whether or not you can play
Sudden Reversal on your own turn, and it can only be played during
another Methuselah's turn.

Comments please. Thanks.

--

> > Mike plays Minion Tap.
> > Brian plays Sudden Reversal to cancel the Minion Tap
> >
> > Mike plays Sudden Reversal to cancel Brian's Sudden Reversal.

point 1- mike cannot play a master out of turn during his turn
(barring special text on the card -example : Contengency planning)

point 2- mike just played a master card. (If a card in play grants him a
second maser phase action, it's okay to play a second one, as long as you
don't violate point 2)

> > Is that a legal play? We finally decided that it was, and that the
> > Minion Tap was successful.
>
> No.

As LSJ stated, you made a mistake. Brian's sudden could have been suddened
by another player than mike, though =)

> > The only thing I was not sure about is whether or not you can play
> > Sudden Reversal on your own turn, and it can only be played during
> > another Methuselah's turn.
>
> See 1.6.2.3

Errmm this is a shorter way to say "that means you cannot do so since the
rulebook clearly states so."
LSJ likes short answers, you know ;)
